title: Parking Brake Cable Adjustment
introduction:
This adjustment sets the cable using the clearance between the rear caliper operating levers and their stops. I use that measured gap as the referee: how impressive the cabin handle feels is not the measurement in this procedure.

The sequence matters. Make the initial setting, fully cycle the parking brake, then make the final setting. The illustrations connect the magenta adjustment nut at the underbody cable equalizer with the lever-to-stop gap at the calipers. This is a cable adjustment, not a hydraulic brake service or a diagnosis of every parking-brake complaint.

items.name: Disable remote start and secure the key
items.detail:
Position the car at the hoist on a hard, level surface. Apply the parking brake and chock all wheels that remain on the ground before releasing the service brake or selecting Neutral.

If fitted, disable remote start through the Central Display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Do this before working around or underneath the car. If ignition power is needed, keep the valid key inside and, from known OFF, press and release the start/stop button without pressing the brake or clutch pedal.

For an automatic, keep the valid key inside. Before shifting out of P, establish engine-off ignition ON: if it is OFF, release both pedals and press and release the start/stop button once; if it is already ON from the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. With the service brake depressed and the parking brake and chocks still restraining the car, select Neutral. For a manual, select Neutral while retaining the parking brake and chocks.

Once positioning and settings are complete, leave the engine off. With the car restrained, release the pedals and, if the ignition is ON, press and release the button once to turn it OFF. If it is already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle and prevent anyone from operating the controls. Unexpected starting can cause serious injury or death. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Arrange a suitable hoist and access to the handbrake
items.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, on a hard, level working surface. Plan a securely supported working height that provides safe underside access while allowing the cabin handbrake to be reached by someone standing on the floor beside the open door. Nobody should climb into the raised vehicle. If both requirements cannot be met, arrange suitable workshop access before beginning.

items.name: Capacity and lifting points
items.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle weight, including cargo and modifications. The supporting drawing places the lifting locations along the body sides, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Locate the triangles stamped into the body sheet metal or frame and position the lift arms at the specified points. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious injury. Review [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631).

items.name: Avoid contact damage
items.detail: Before lifting, position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped; avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

items.name: Support and movement precautions
items.detail: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; it can lower unexpectedly and cause serious injury. Use floor stands after jacking. The vehicle's emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire, and applying jack pressure to either bumper will damage its cover. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are elevated; incorrect lift-arm placement or powered wheels touching the ground can cause unintended movement and serious injury or death.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp components. Failure to use this protection may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Avoid brake-dust exposure
items.detail: Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). Do not breathe friction-component dust or blow it from components or storage containers with compressed air. If dust removal is needed, use government-approved techniques. The dust may present cancer and lung-disease hazards, irritate skin, eyes and the respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions, or contribute to other chronic effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Failure to observe these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

edits.why: The equipment table identifies the tool used to measure the caliper lever clearance.

edits.text:
Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist.
Refer to: [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The hoist provides access to the underbody cable adjustment and the rear caliper levers. Use the stamped lifting-point triangles described in the preparation requirements rather than choosing a convenient-looking underbody surface. Keep the parking brake applied and restrain wheels while they remain on the ground during positioning. Before releasing the parking brake for adjustment, establish that the car is securely supported on the hoist with all wheels clear of the ground. Keep the parking brake fully released during each lever-gap measurement; apply and release it only for the specified cycling step. Have a person standing on the floor beside the open door operate the handbrake at the planned safe height; nobody should climb into the raised cabin. Keep everyone clear of cables and caliper levers whenever the handbrake moves.

edits.text: Tighten the parking brake cable adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 2.0 mm away from their stops. Use the General Equipment: Feeler Gauge to measure the gap between each lever and its stop.
edits.why: The main drawing identifies the adjustment nut on the threaded cable at the equalizer. The inset shows the clearance between the caliper's operating lever and its fixed stop. Check both sides; the stated endpoint is reached when either lever, or both levers, has the specified clearance.

edits.text: Fully apply and then fully release the parking brake 5 times.
edits.why: This operates the cable and caliper-lever mechanism between the initial and final settings. Finish with the handle released before making the next measurement. Stop underbody work and clear hands and tools before the floor-standing operator cycles the handle. Keep ignition OFF and the key outside; resume measuring only once the operator has stopped with the handbrake fully released.

edits.text: Tighten the parking brake cable adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 1.0 mm away from their stops. Use the General Equipment: Feeler Gauge to measure the lever-to-stop gaps.
edits.why:
This is the final measured setting after cycling the mechanism. Use the same lever and fixed-stop surfaces shown in the illustration; the requirement remains either lever or both, rather than an added requirement for identical gaps on both sides. After completing the final measurement, remove the gauge and tools and clear everyone from underneath. Have the floor-standing operator apply the parking brake; nobody enters the raised cabin. Then lower the car, restoring ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground. Keep the vehicle secured; the measured adjustment is not a diagnosis of any remaining parking-brake fault.

Once the car is fully on its tires, with the parking brake applied and wheel chocks in place, restore the transmission from service Neutral to its parked position: P for an automatic, or a parking gear for a manual.

If the automatic requires ignition power, return the valid key to the cabin, switch from known OFF to engine-off ON without pressing a pedal, then depress the service brake and select P. With the parking brake and chocks holding the car, release the pedals and switch the ignition OFF again.

Finish with the engine off, ignition OFF and key removed from the vehicle. Confirm that all tools are accounted for and the hoist arms are clear.

editorialRevision.scope: Explicit safe ground-to-supported-hoist/released-parking-brake and return transitions implement supplied GeneralSafety/lifting requirements. Editorial operational inference, not verbatim Ford instruction. All adjustment actions/2.0mm/five cycles/1.0mm and either-lever criterion unchanged. Removed inherited engine-list introduction unsupported by runtime primary; actual cable/caliper arrangement and all measurements retained. Supplemental owner controls and approved same-primary practical counterpart supply complete known-state Neutral/parked finish and safely reachable floor-standing handbrake operation, preserved privately.
